episode.title: Sunlight Takes 8 Minutes to Reach Us
episode.central_question: What does the eight-minute delay of sunlight tell us about the universe and about life on Earth?

beats.name: Earth at scale
beats.because: Start with the size of home.

beats.name: The travel time
beats.because: Distance is easy to draw. Time is harder to feel.

beats.name: The Sun
beats.because: Now scale up: the Sun is far larger and far farther.

beats.name: The eight-minute gap
beats.because: Light is a clock. It shows us what happened in the past.

beats.name: Life on Earth
beats.because: Eight minutes is a fact about light. The bigger story is what sunlight does.

beats.name: The nearest other star
beats.because: Our Sun is not alone. The next star is much farther.

beats.name: The closing question
beats.because: Light always shows us a little of the past.

shots.voiceover: Right now, the sunlight on your face left the Sun about eight minutes ago.

shots.voiceover: Hold that picture in mind, because every distance in this episode is measured against it.

claims.text: Sunlight takes about 8 min 20 s to reach Earth

shots.voiceover: Every image of the Sun you have ever seen is a snapshot of a few minutes ago.

visual.search_query: Sun image held, slow push

visual.search_query: 3D visualization: Sun dims in the frame, clock overlay
visual.credit: Our visualization, Solar System Scope textures where used (CC BY 4.0)

shots.voiceover: You would not notice anything for eight minutes.

visual.search_query: 3D visualization: Earth in daylight, clock running
visual.credit: Our visualization, Solar System Scope textures where used (CC BY 4.0)

shots.voiceover: The sky would look normal, the warmth on your skin would feel the same.

visual.search_query: 3D visualization: Earth in daylight, calm pan
visual.credit: Our visualization, Solar System Scope textures where used (CC BY 4.0)

shots.voiceover: The light would keep arriving as if nothing had happened.

shots.voiceover: The bigger story is what sunlight does once it arrives.

visual.search_query: NASA Earth from orbit, real image

shots.voiceover: Almost every food chain on our planet starts with it.

visual.search_query: Plants and vegetation from orbit, real image

shots.voiceover: Plants, algae and some bacteria capture that energy and turn it into food.

visual.search_query: Phytoplankton bloom, real image

shots.voiceover: Animals eat them, and other animals eat those animals.

visual.search_query: Food web scene, real photo

shots.voiceover: Seasons, weather and the water cycle are all driven by the energy that arrives in those eight minutes.

visual.credit: Our visualization, Solar System Scope textures where used (CC BY 4.0)
